assessment: The incumbent offers a plausible opportunity to check completeness and fit during assembly, while removable slots retain rearrangeability; these benefits are not causally demonstrated. Performance remains insufficient: median combined time is 11 minutes, five partition problems were reported, and seven of ten observed customers succeeded unaided. D2-O6 limits an account that full assembly inherently takes too long: repeated three-compartment orders took seven to nine minutes, while every extreme delay occurred in mixed batches. Layout complexity and switching remain confounded. No damage claims alone cannot establish packaging effectiveness.

openings.claim: Order-specific reusable parts trays may reduce selection and checking delays and partition omissions while retaining full workshop assembly.
openings.delta: Separate each accepted order’s required parts and exterior color before insertion instead of selecting repeatedly from shared shape bins.
openings.prediction: Against the incumbent on matched mixed-layout runs, selection/checking time and independently counted kit errors decrease without a comparable insertion-time change.
openings.probe: Using reusable sample parts within the 15-sample allowance, alternate incumbent and tray runs across both workers and accepted layout/color variants. Time selection, insertion, checking and packing separately, including tray preparation; independently inventory every completed kit. Check total cost and delivery impact before pilot adoption.
assumptions: Trays can be made within 500 initially and 0.40 recurring per order.
Trials fit available working time; ordered components, footprint, capacity, removability and colors remain identical.

openings.claim: Does locating the short partition in the ordered layout, rather than physical insertion difficulty, explain the observed requests for help?
openings.delta: Replace the generic three-layout diagram with an order-specific diagram clearly locating the short partition.
openings.prediction: If layout interpretation is limiting, correct unaided short-partition placement improves while insertion retries after correct positioning remain similar.
openings.probe: Assign ten participants to matched layout groups receiving either diagram with otherwise identical organizers. Observe placement decisions, insertion retries, requests for help and successful ordered arrangement within ten minutes. Treat this as a small diagnostic, not proof of 90% pilot success.
assumptions: The replacement diagram fits the existing print allowance and delivery schedule.
Equivalent physical parts and balanced layouts make the comparison interpretable.
